A

.

Job Description:
Enterprise Independent Testing (EIT) has established itself as the enterprise utility for testing all end-to-end processes on behalf of the Second Line of Defense, Frontline Units (FLUs), and Control Functions (CFs), enabling more efficient and effective testing.
This role is responsible for developing capabilities such as models, analytical tools, and testing scripts that provide timely, actionable insights into the operational health of Bank of America’s processes. Key responsibilities include working with process owners to understand data, process flows, and controls; identifying risks; and designing effective testing and monitoring. Job expectations include creating methodologies to evaluate process and control effectiveness and compliance with laws, rules, and policies.
Responsibilities:
Embodies EIT core skills: critical thinking, decisiveness, enterprise mindset, proactivity, project management, risk management, adaptability, collaboration, customer and client focus, effective written and verbal communication, and control rigor and discipline
Partners effectively with process and data owners in the FLUs/CFs, risk managers, Global Compliance Operational Risk (GCOR), and various teams within EIT that provide operational, data sourcing, and technology infrastructure support. Methodology outputs are used to drive process improvements and timely detection and reporting of errors
Uses methodology outputs, including analytical tools and testing scripts, to drive process improvements and timely detection of errors
Communicates effectively to explain the rationale, methodology details, and results to a broad set of audiences, including key senior stakeholders across the Bank, auditors, and regulators
Applies experience in process and operational excellence
Reviews test builds, maintenance, and quality assessments
Oversees the identification and handling of issue escalation/resolution to prevent delays in delivery and identify and leverage opportunities for automation where possible
Interacts extensively with internal or external contacts to identify, research, analyze and resolve complex problems
Ensures effectiveness and compliance with laws, rules, and policies.
Required Education & Experience:
Bachelor’s degree or above in fields including, but not limited to, Finance, Economics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Statistics, Process and Mechanical Engineering, Operations Research, Data Science, Accounting, or Business Administration, or equivalent work experience
2 Years of relevant work experience
Required Skills:
Process Design: Ability to understand how work is executed within an organization, evaluate efficiencies, and identify areas for overall process improvement and growth

Test Reporting: Ability to produce testing results, reporting, and data-driven insights for the test inventory
Test Development Life Cycle: Understands the end-to-end test development life cycle, from test request to development, execution, and dissemination of results. Collaborates with cross-functional teams to meet testing objectives
Programming Languages: Strong computational programming skills using programming languages or scripts such as Spark, R, C, Java, YAML, and others

description_preview:
Please note that this position is based on our campus in Madison, WI, and requires relocation to the area. We recruit nationally and provide financial relocation assistance.
Code that saves lives.
As a software developer at Epic, you’ll write software that impacts the lives of 325 million patients around the world. Working in your own office, surrounded by thousands of high-caliber developers, you’ll use modern development methodologies and employ user-centered design, analytics, and machine learning tools to drive innovation in healthcare. Using leading-edge technologies and languages like JS, TS, and C#, you’ll invent better ways to reduce medical errors, streamline record sharing between hospitals, and provide the quality of care a patient deserves. Learn more about our team at https://careers.epic.com/jobs/softwaredevelopment/.
Write software for the most innovative health systems on the planet.
The top-ranked health systems in U.S. News and World Report are Epic customers. Our community includes major systems like the Mayo Clinic, Johns Hopkins, Cleveland Clinic, and Kaiser Permanente, as well as leading academic medical centers at the University of Wisconsin, University of Michigan, University of California, University of Texas, The Ohio State University, and many more.
Live affordably in a city known for its rising tech talent.
Epic is located just outside Madison, Wisconsin, the second fastest growing market for tech talent in the United States and home to the state capital and the University of Wisconsin. Madison, a city surrounded by water, has received accolades for being the greenest city in America (NerdWallet), the best city for renters (SmartAsset), the fittest city in America (Fitbit), and the third best metro in the US for young professionals (Forbes Advisor).
More than just important work
.
Our uniquely themed campus was designed to heighten your ability to get stuff done in your office, a conference room, or by the fireplace in a comfy chair. All meals are restaurant-quality but cost only a few dollars, and they’re prepared by a team comprised of kitchen talent from restaurants around the country. And, after five years here, you’ll earn a four-week sabbatical anywhere in the world. Staff have kayaked in Patagonia, attended a Beyoncé concert in Ireland, built a library in Tanzania, and run a marathon in Antarctica.
We offer comprehensive benefits to keep you healthy and happy as you grow in your life and career, and your merit-based compensation will reflect the impact your work has on the company and our customers. You'll also be eligible for annual raises and bonuses, as well as stock grants, which give you an even greater stake in the success of Epic and our customers. Healthcare is global, and building the best ideas from around the world into Epic software is a point of pride. As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we know that inclusive teams design software that supports the delivery of quality care for all patients, so diversity, equity, and inclusion are written into our principles. Please see our full non-discrimination statement at https://careers.epic.com/EEO.

BS/BA or greater in Computer Science, Mathematics, Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field
A history of academic excellence or professional success

We’re looking for fast learners with engineering or problem-solving backgrounds, who are comfortable diving deep with clients.
What you'll actually do
Sit in client conversations, listen for what they need rather than what they said, and turn it into a build plan.
Build voice agents and YAML-defined workflows on the Attune platform.
Write test scenarios that try to break your own work, including the edge cases nobody asked about.
Debug live agent behavior — what the agent heard, what it decided, why it went wrong — and fix it.
Own deployments outright. You are the owner: the client relationship, the requirements, the build, the tests, the go-live. On the genuinely novel deployments, you'll work alongside a Forward Deployed Engineer who owns the hardest technical calls.
Feed what you learn back into the product. You'll be closer to real client pain than almost anyone at the company, and we'll expect you to say so loudly.
What we're looking for
Required:
An engineering or problem-solving background — this can be a CS or engineering degree, a quantitative field, or a demonstrable track record of teaching yourself technical systems because you needed them to work.
Comfort reading and writing structured configuration and reasoning about conditional logic and state.
The ability to hold a technical conversation with a non-technical client without either condescending or over-promising.
Genuine curiosity about failure modes. The best people in this role are the ones who ask "what happens if the caller interrupts here?" before anyone prompts them.
Willingness to be wrong quickly and in public. Our feedback cycles are short.
Helpful but not required:
Experience in implementation engineering, sales engineering, technical delivery, automation, QA, or analytics engineering.
Any exposure to conversational AI, IVR, telephony, or contact center systems.
Python or scripting for one-off data wrangling and testing.
Client-facing experience at an early-stage company, where the job description was mostly a suggestion.
What we're explicitly not requiring:
A software engineering degree or significant software development experience.
Prior voice AI experience. We will teach you this — it's the part we're good at.
Levels
FDSE I
is for people with roughly 0–2 years of experience. You'll build under review, own your test coverage, and grow into requirements work and then into owning deployments yourself. We expect to invest heavily in you for the first few months.
FDSE II
is for people with roughly 2–5 years in an adjacent technical delivery role. You'll own standard deployments solo from the first client call to go-live, and we'll expect you to resolve ambiguity rather than escalate it — and to recognize the cases where escalating is the right call.
Apply once — we'll figure out the level together during the process.
Where this goes
There is a real path from FDSE II into Forward Deployed Engineer and Solution Engineering leadership, and people who want it will get direct support and mentorship toward it. There is also a real career at FDSE II and beyond for people who'd rather deepen client ownership than move toward platform work.

Engineers have the freedom to create a lot of impact for our customers. The role requires high agency and comfort with change. Work in React, Redux, Ruby, Rails, Postgres, and potentially Scala, Python, and Go to solve problems for our customers.

Jam with Product Managers, Designers, Ops, and other Engineers every day to shape the direction of our products.

Partly is connecting the world's parts, and we're doing that by building the AI infrastructure layer for the global repair industry, starting with the $2tn automotive market. Our frontier model, Interpreter, is the world's first AI purpose-built to understand vehicle damage and the parts needed to fix it. Thousands of businesses across the global repair supply chain already rely on it.
Founded by ex-Rocket Lab engineers, we've tripled in size in the last 18 months and have recently raised a $50m Series B led by DST Global (Anthropic, Airbnb, Meta, TikTok, Spotify) and including Blackbird Ventures (Canva, CultureAmp etc.), WNDR, Activant Capital, Icehouse Ventures, Square Peg, Airtree, and Ecliptic Venture Capital. We're headquartered in Austin, with offices in New Zealand and London.
We're continuing to build a world-class team ensuring Partly is a place where people can do the best work of their lives. We're proud of the culture we've built, and our values are lived throughout every experience.
Want to learn more about the problems we're solving and the culture we're building at Partly? Hear directly from our team here: https://shorturl.at/iAFUX
💻 What will you do
Build, not just specify. Prototype new product iterations yourself using AI-assisted and LLM-assisted tooling—fast, disposable, real. Treat the prototype as the hypothesis and put it in front of real customers before writing the spec. Ship production code, instrument it, and watch how it actually gets used.
Stay close to customers. Spend time where the work happens. Understand what estimators, parts managers, and others actually do, where they lose time, and what "better" would feel like. This is a core weekly activity, not an occasional input.
Reconcile signal. Combine what you see with what the data says, and reconcile the two when they disagree. Turn that understanding straight into what you build next.
Own the outcome. Steer by your surface's metrics; adoption and value delivered are yours. Make the call on priority and explain the reasoning, especially when the answer is no. When something is broken, own it, diagnose it precisely, and fix it.
Make the trade-off. Weigh product impact against engineering effort in the same breath, and find the cheaper path to the same outcome.
Build the agentic experience. Move your surface from manual operation toward supervised delegation: capture intent, decide where the human stays in the loop, and earn trust step by step so users never lose the thread of a high-stakes job.
Hold the craft. The surface feels fast, clear, and considered. You push back when something doesn't feel right, even when it technically works.
Raise the bar. Pair with SW Engineers on the harder systems work behind your surface, and contribute beyond your boundary: shared components, product craft, and what excellent building looks like here as the team grows.
🥷 Your skills
Non-negotiables
You ship end to end: A track record of taking features from idea to production, code included, with clear accountability for whether they worked. Roughly 3+ years building and shipping software in production.
Genuine customer obsession: A real habit of spending time with users in their work context, with a track record of that depth driving what you build.
Product taste and craft: The bar is experiences that feel effortless to time-pressured, non-technical users across fragmented, high-stakes workflows. Functional is not the finish line.
A point of view on agentic product design: How an experience moves from manual operation to supervised delegation, and how automation earns user trust gradually rather than all at once.
You build rapid prototypes yourself, with AI-assisted tools as a first instinct for testing an idea.
Solid full-stack engineering with a frontend lean: Production-quality code and sound fundamentals. Systems-specialist depth is not the point of the role.
Trade-off fluency: You weigh product impact against engineering effort and often find a cheaper route to the same result.
Strong analytical instinct: You define the metric, build the view, read it, and act without waiting for a data team.
You operate well in ambiguity and autonomy, and shape the problem rather than waiting for a spec.
Strong signals we look for
Shipped AI-assisted or agent-driven features in production, particularly where the human stays in the loop.
Built for a multi-persona, operational, or workflow-heavy B2B product.
Founder background, or early employee at a startup that scaled materially.
You've killed or radically changed something you personally believed in and can explain why.
Bonus
Domain knowledge in automotive, the parts aftermarket, repair, or insurance claims.
Marketplace or network experience, from the demand or supply side.
Rust, or genuine eagerness to learn it. It is part of our stack.
🧭 How you'll think and operate
We're not looking for spec-takers or framework experts. We're looking for someone who thinks like this:
"I sat with a parts manager on Tuesday, saw exactly where the order flow broke, prototyped a fix that afternoon, and three shops were testing it by Friday."
"I could build the 'right' version in three weeks, or a version that answers the actual question in two days. I shipped the two-day one, learned it was wrong, and saved myself the three weeks."
"Here's what the usage data shows. Here's what I think it means. Here's the change I made, and here's how I'll know if I was wrong."
"This is my surface. If it feels clunky, that's on me. Let me show you exactly what's clunky and what I'm doing about it."
Speed, ownership, and judgment are the basel

description_preview:
In today's dynamic worksites, seamless collaboration between people and machines is essential. FORT's platform ensures safe, secure, and dynamic control that surpasses legacy systems and next-generation AI capabilities.
While autonomous machines offer significant advantages, they also introduce new safety challenges. FORT addresses these concerns by providing solutions such as the Wireless E-Stop, which allows operators to instantly stop any machine from a safe distance, enhancing safety during emergencies.
Additionally, FORT's Safe Remote Control enables operators to manage heavy machinery remotely, reducing the risk of accidents and improving visibility.
By ensuring communications integrity across any network, FORT empowers customers to protect their most valuable assets—people, data, and machines—ensuring they remain safe and secure.
As an Embedded Software Engineer II, you will own specific components of our embedded stack, working close to the hardware on the real-time firmware that our safety devices depend on. Most of your time will be spent in RTOS environments (Zephyr and FreeRTOS) and on bare-metal targets, architecting safety-critical systems where reliability is a hard requirement. You will also work with our Embedded Linux platforms where the two worlds meet, so you will be comfortable moving between constrained real-time targets and richer application environments.
What You'll Do
Build the Core:
Design and implement robust C/C++ firmware for safety-critical embedded devices.
Real-Time Architecture:
Architect and implement RTOS-based firmware on Zephyr and FreeRTOS, including task and scheduling design, ISR handling, inter-task communication, memory and stack budgeting, and deterministic timing analysis.
Bare-Metal and Drivers:
Write low-level peripheral drivers and board support code, and bring up new silicon from reset vector through to a running application.
Platform Integration:
Interface RTOS devices with our Embedded Linux user-space applications, ensuring reliable communication and consistent behavior across the product.
Pipeline & Quality:
Maintain and improve CI/CD pipelines (GitLab) to automate testing, including on-target and hardware-in-the-loop test execution.
Hardware Integration:
Bring up new hardware, debug complex issues using JTAG/GDB, and optimize for latency, power, and memory footprint.
Safety Compliance:
Collaborate with the safety team to ensure code adheres to rigorous standards (IEC 61508) while maintaining development velocity.
What You Bring
Experience:
3-5 years of hands-on embedded software development, with a substantial portion on RTOS or bare-metal targets.
Core Languages:
Strong proficiency in C, along with working proficiency in C++.
RTOS Knowledge:
Solid production experience with an RTOS such as Zephyr, FreeRTOS, ThreadX, or similar, including scheduling, synchronization primitives, and interrupt-driven design.
Microcontroller Fluency:
Comfort working directly with MCU peripherals, datasheets, reference manuals, linker scripts, and startup code.
Linux Exposure:
Familiarity with Embedded Linux user-space development, sufficient to integrate and debug across the RTOS and Linux boundary.
Connectivity:
Familiarity with IP networking protocols and standard interfaces (UART, SPI, I2C, USB, CAN).
Tooling:
Experience with Python for scripting/automation and familiarity with CI/CD workflows.
Debugging:
Comfort using oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, JTAG, and GDB to troubleshoot hard-to-find bugs.
Education:
B.S. in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or equivalent experience.
Bonus Points
Experience with Zephyr specifically, including devicetree, Kconfig, and west-based workflows.
Experience with wireless stacks (BLE, ISM, Wi-Fi) on constrained devices.
Background in Functional Safety (FuSa) or working in regulated industries (Medical, Automotive, Aerospace).
Low-level Linux knowledge of Board Support Packages (BSP) and device drivers.
Familiarity with static analysis, MISRA C, or other coding standards used in safety-critical development.
Base Compensation can range from $125,000 to $150,000 based on experience & location.

At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!
This role is part of Advanced Concepts and Enterprise Engineering (ACE), supporting Blue Origin’s mission of millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. The team fosters innovation and drives engineering workflows of the future, shared solutions and standards, simplicity and lower costs, and manufacturable design.
This role is part of the Advanced Concepts and Enterprise Engineering (ACE) team, which supports Blue Origin's mission of millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. Our team fosters innovation and drives the engineering workflows of the future by developing shared solutions and standards that emphasize simplicity, lower costs, and manufacturable design.
Job Summary
As a Systems Engineer II focused on a Vehicle Digital Twin, you will be at the forefront of developing a connected, data-driven representation of our vehicle using NVIDIA Omniverse. In this hands-on role, you will connect system architecture, requirements, CAD geometry, analysis models, test evidence, and operational data into a single, traceable digital thread. This position uniquely combines systems engineering fundamentals with software automation, model integration, and the practical application of advanced artificial intelligence tools.
You will own scoped integrations and work products, partnering with senior engineers and multidisciplinary teams. The ideal candidate is comfortable moving between system models, 3D/CAD data, code, and engineering evidence, with a talent for turning ambiguous needs into testable and maintainable solutions.
Responsibilities Include But Are Not Limited To
Develop and maintain Blue Origin Aerobrake Digital Twin capabilities in NVIDIA Omniverse, including data-driven 3D scenes, engineering metadata, behaviors, and reusable integration components.
Build and improve OpenUSD-based workflows that ingest and organize PTC Creo or other CAD geometry while preserving configuration, provenance, coordinate systems, and product-structure metadata.
Connect Dassault Systèmes Cameo and Teamwork Cloud system models to the Digital Twin, ensuring requirements, interfaces, functions, verification evidence, and design decisions remain traceable to authoritative sources.
Develop Python-based APIs, connectors, and data pipelines that link analysis, simulation, test, telemetry, and engineering repositories to the Digital Twin.
Support the correlation of digital models with physical test data by defining acceptance criteria, investigating model-to-test differences, and documenting assumptions, limitations, and uncertainty.
Utilize advanced AI-assisted engineering and software-development tools (e.g., Codex, Claude Code, or equivalent) to accelerate integration, automation, and documentation, while independently verifying outputs and maintaining configuration control.
Apply systems engineering fundamentals to decompose needs, define interfaces and data contracts, manage technical risks, and plan verification and validation for Digital Twin capabilities.
Collaborate with guidance, navigation, and control; structures; thermal; avionics; software; test; manufacturing; and mission operations teams to deliver useful Digital Twin workflows.
Participate in agile planning, demonstrations, technical reviews, and retrospectives; communicate progress, tradeoffs, and blockers clearly to all stakeholders.
Minimum Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in Systems Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical discipline.
2+ years of relevant professional experience in systems engineering, digital engineering, digital twins, simulation, or software integration. An advanced degree may be considered in lieu of experience.
Hands-on experience with Dassault Systèmes Cameo or MagicDraw and Teamwork Cloud to develop, manage, or review system models in a collaborative environment.
Experience using PTC Creo or another production CAD tool and working with engineering geometry, assemblies, and coordinate systems.
Programming or automation experience (preferably Python), including version control, debugging, and integration with APIs or structured engineering data.
Demonstrated practical use of advanced AI-assisted engineering or coding tools (e.g., Codex, Claude Code, or equivalent), with strong judgment for validating generated content.
Working knowledge of digital thread concepts and systems engineering fundamentals, including requirements, interfaces, traceability, configuration management, and V&V.
Ability to work effectively across disciplines, communicate technical information clearly, and execute scoped work in a fast-paced, collaborative environment.
Preferred Qualifications
Hands-on experience with NVIDIA Omniverse, Omniverse Kit, OpenUSD, or real-time 3D simulation and visualization workflows.
Experience building or operating a digital twin that links authoritative product definitions with simulation, test, or operational data.
Experience with MATLAB/Simulink, ANSYS, computational fluid dynamics, 6-DOF simulation, or hardware/software-in-the-loop test environments.
Familiarity with GitLab, CI/CD, containers, cloud platforms, databases, or event-driven data pipelines.
Experience developing aerospace vehicles or other complex, safety-critical products through their full lifecycle (design, integration, test, and operations).
Master's degree or PhD in a relevant engineering or technical field.
Active SECRET clearance or the ability to obtain a TS/SCI clearance.

At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!
This role is part of Advanced Concepts and Enterprise Engineering (ACE), supporting Blue Origin’s mission of millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. The team fosters innovation and drives engineering workflows of the future, shared solutions and standards, simplicity and lower costs, and manufacturable design.
This role is part of the Advanced Concepts and Enterprise Engineering (ACE) team, which supports Blue Origin's mission of millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. Our team fosters innovation and drives the engineering workflows of the future by developing shared solutions and standards that emphasize simplicity, lower costs, and manufacturable design.
Job Summary
As a Systems Engineer II focused on a Vehicle Digital Twin, you will be at the forefront of developing a connected, data-driven representation of our vehicle using NVIDIA Omniverse. In this hands-on role, you will connect system architecture, requirements, CAD geometry, analysis models, test evidence, and operational data into a single, traceable digital thread. This position uniquely combines systems engineering fundamentals with software automation, model integration, and the practical application of advanced artificial intelligence tools.
You will own scoped integrations and work products, partnering with senior engineers and multidisciplinary teams. The ideal candidate is comfortable moving between system models, 3D/CAD data, code, and engineering evidence, with a talent for turning ambiguous needs into testable and maintainable solutions.
Responsibilities Include But Are Not Limited To
Develop and maintain Blue Origin Aerobrake Digital Twin capabilities in NVIDIA Omniverse, including data-driven 3D scenes, engineering metadata, behaviors, and reusable integration components.
Build and improve OpenUSD-based workflows that ingest and organize PTC Creo or other CAD geometry while preserving configuration, provenance, coordinate systems, and product-structure metadata.
Connect Dassault Systèmes Cameo and Teamwork Cloud system models to the Digital Twin, ensuring requirements, interfaces, functions, verification evidence, and design decisions remain traceable to authoritative sources.
Develop Python-based APIs, connectors, and data pipelines that link analysis, simulation, test, telemetry, and engineering repositories to the Digital Twin.
Support the correlation of digital models with physical test data by defining acceptance criteria, investigating model-to-test differences, and documenting assumptions, limitations, and uncertainty.
Utilize advanced AI-assisted engineering and software-development tools (e.g., Codex, Claude Code, or equivalent) to accelerate integration, automation, and documentation, while independently verifying outputs and maintaining configuration control.
Apply systems engineering fundamentals to decompose needs, define interfaces and data contracts, manage technical risks, and plan verification and validation for Digital Twin capabilities.
Collaborate with guidance, navigation, and control; structures; thermal; avionics; software; test; manufacturing; and mission operations teams to deliver useful Digital Twin workflows.
Participate in agile planning, demonstrations, technical reviews, and retrospectives; communicate progress, tradeoffs, and blockers clearly to all stakeholders.
Minimum Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in Systems Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical discipline.
2+ years of relevant professional experience in systems engineering, digital engineering, digital twins, simulation, or software integration. An advanced degree may be considered in lieu of experience.
Hands-on experience with Dassault Systèmes Cameo or MagicDraw and Teamwork Cloud to develop, manage, or review system models in a collaborative environment.
Experience using PTC Creo or another production CAD tool and working with engineering geometry, assemblies, and coordinate systems.
Programming or automation experience (preferably Python), including version control, debugging, and integration with APIs or structured engineering data.
Demonstrated practical use of advanced AI-assisted engineering or coding tools (e.g., Codex, Claude Code, or equivalent), with strong judgment for validating generated content.
Working knowledge of digital thread concepts and systems engineering fundamentals, including requirements, interfaces, traceability, configuration management, and V&V.
Ability to work effectively across disciplines, communicate technical information clearly, and execute scoped work in a fast-paced, collaborative environment.
Preferred Qualifications
Hands-on experience with NVIDIA Omniverse, Omniverse Kit, OpenUSD, or real-time 3D simulation and visualization workflows.
Experience building or operating a digital twin that links authoritative product definitions with simulation, test, or operational data.
Experience with MATLAB/Simulink, ANSYS, computational fluid dynamics, 6-DOF simulation, or hardware/software-in-the-loop test environments.
Familiarity with GitLab, CI/CD, containers, cloud platforms, databases, or event-driven data pipelines.
Experience developing aerospace vehicles or other complex, safety-critical products through their full lifecycle (design, integration, test, and operations).
Master's degree or PhD in a relevant engineering or technical field.
Active SECRET clearance or the ability to obtain a TS/SCI clearance.
Special Men

Bigge Crane and Rigging has been elevating America since 1916. Job Overview
We are looking for a Salesforce Developer to join our Business Systems team and help build and maintain the Salesforce environments behind Bigge's SalesPro platform — a custom-built Salesforce environment supporting crane rental, sales, and field operations across 20+ branches nationwide. This is a hands-on development role focused on writing solid Apex and Lightning Web Components, and increasingly, applying AI tools to work faster and smarter.
This role reports directly to the Senior Salesforce Technical Lead, who sets platform direction and reviews major design decisions. You'll take ownership of well-scoped features and fixes end-to-end, with support available for the harder architectural calls.
The position is ideally based in Houston, TX, with a hybrid in-office and remote schedule. However, remote candidates may be considered for the right fit.

Write, test, and maintain Apex classes, triggers, and batch jobs, following governor limit, order-of-execution, and bulkification best practices.
Build and maintain Lightning Web Components using wire methods and reactive properties.
Build declarative automation using Flows and validation rules for day-to-day business requirements.
Implement custom objects, fields, relationships, and page layouts to support evolving business requirements.
Troubleshoot and resolve day-to-day bugs and performance issues, escalating architectural or cross-system issues to the senior developer/technical lead.
Use Git and Salesforce DX for source-driven development, following established branching and sandbox conventions.
Deploy changes through existing CI/CD pipelines in Azure DevOps.
Maintain data quality on assigned work, including deduplication and intake validation.
Use AI coding assistants (e.g., Claude, Cursor) to speed up day-to-day development work.
Participate in agile 2-week sprints — story pointing, backlog grooming, and sprint planning.
Requirements
3–5 years of Salesforce development experience with Apex and LWC as primary, daily-use skills.
Working understanding of governor limits, order of execution, and bulkification.
Familiarity with Git-based, source-driven development; exposure to SFDX and CI/CD pipelines a plus.
Comfortable working in agile 2-week sprints, including backlog grooming and story pointing.
